additional_info.subject: SI Charge D Meter Values
additional_info.body:
Hello SI Emobility,
I’m encountering something with an SI Charge D for which I’m looking for some clarity.   This pertains to the meterStart, meterStop and the energy register.
With the charger following what I believe is referred to as ‘Zero Based’ meterStart’s, using 0 as the meterStart and having the total Wh delivered in the meterStop, I’m running into a couple of challenges:
Across 10 sessions, I’m seeing inconsistencies in the value provided in the meterStop, relative to the cumulative energy derived from the meter register alone.  There are multiple instances in which the cumulative energy from the first meter until the last is already more than the value found in the meterStop, and that is without including the energy between the start of transaction and first meter, or the energy between the last meter and the stop of transaction.  The only conclusion I can come to is that the energy is under calculated, perhaps for all the sessions.
To apply Time of Use rates, the energy must be grouped into quarter hour groups which may each have different rates.   This Zero Based approach results in a need to approximate the energy delivered in between the start and first meter, as well as between the last meter and the stop message, not being able to determine that from the OCPP messages in the way it can be done with the meter register approach.
On individual sessions the differences are relatively minor, however over the course of a month with many sessions, the aggregate total of missing energy could grow to a material amount when providing Tariff cost information.
My ask is whether this is expected behavior, that the meterStop may reflect a lower amount than the cumulative energy delivered, and whether there is any recommended approach to determine the energy delivered between the start of transaction & the first meter, as well as between the last meter and the stop of transaction when using this Zero Based method.
Charger serial number: 160342780
